Please review the following manuscript I wrote.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'fitz', 'pypdfium2', 'PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'Page {i+1}: {len(t)} chars')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
for p in [6,7,8,18]:
 print('\\n=== FIGURE TEXT PAGE',p+1,'===\\n')
 t=r.pages[p].extract_text()
 print(t[:17000])
PY"

strengths: The paper presents a useful combination of density-ratio Bayesian optimization and graph-based semi-supervised learning. Exploiting the geometry of available candidate pools is well motivated, and the relationship to BORE, LFBO, label propagation, and label spreading is explained clearly.

The evaluation includes synthetic functions, tabular hyperparameter optimization, NATS-Bench, and an image-embedding search task. Comparisons against multiple BORE/LFBO classifiers and GP acquisitions, with 20 repetitions and standard errors, provide substantial empirical evidence. Figures 2, 3, and 6 show promising gains on several benchmarks.

The appendices examine bandwidth, sampling distributions, unlabeled sample counts, pool subsampling, and threshold ratios. These analyses, together with pseudocode and benchmark descriptions, help readers understand the method’s behavior and sensitivity.
weaknesses: The central benefit of semi-supervision is insufficiently isolated. Figure 12 includes a valuable labeled-only comparison, but using no unlabeled data performs better in some cases, notably Bukin6 with label propagation and Branin with label spreading. Moreover, this ablation fixes beta at 0.5, whereas the main experiments learn substantially larger values. Appropriately tuned labeled-only kernel baselines under the main evaluation protocols, together with an ablation of randomized tie-breaking, are needed to separate the contributions of unlabeled data, bandwidth selection, and randomized exploration.

The proposed sampling scheme does not establish the cluster assumption. Truncated Gaussians centered on evaluated inputs can connect points with different threshold-defined labels through high-density regions. Appendix C also does not establish its claimed decision-region expansion and correctly acknowledges that the cited i.i.d. learning bounds do not directly apply to adaptive optimization. Enlarging a high-probability region alone does not demonstrate improved exploration under argmax selection. Consequently, the explanation for alleviating over-exploitation remains conjectural.

Important implementation details remain unspecified, including feature scaling, the clamping factor, propagation tolerance and iteration limit, and the bounds and initialization used to optimize beta. The stated use of L-BFGS-B with 1,000 starts also leaves unclear how acquisition maximization respects arbitrary finite candidate pools and how tree-based baseline acquisitions are optimized. These details materially affect reproducibility and confidence in the comparisons.

Evidence for broader applicability is limited. Continuous optimization is tested only on four two-dimensional functions. The 64-dimensional MNIST experiment uses a representation trained on 440,000 examples to predict the same three-digit labels that define the optimization objective. Although this representation is shared across methods, it supplies substantial task-specific supervision, limiting what the experiment establishes about general high-dimensional black-box optimization.

Practical computational performance is not adequately established. Appendix G usefully compares pool subset sizes, but its timing experiments use a fixed bandwidth and do not compare end-to-end runtime against competing methods. Repeated bandwidth optimization, graph construction, and acquisition optimization should be included when assessing the practical value of the evaluation-count improvements.

A smaller, correctable mathematical inconsistency occurs in Section 4.1: the scalar definition of p_ij normalizes columns, whereas P = D^{-1}W normalizes rows. Together with the transpose in Equation 11, these specify different propagation procedures and should be reconciled with the implementation.
